    How this screen works

    The pipeline reads CVM's public filings (daily NAV/flows, portfolio composition, fund registry) and runs about 19 independent statistical detectors per fund. None are machine-learned — every one is a threshold or z-score check, fast and free of training data, but only as good as its threshold for a given fund type.

    FamilyDetectorsWhat it flags
    Flow / NAVflow z-scores, PL drops, redemption runs, flow-vs-performance divergence statistically unusual captação/resgate or PL moves
    ValuationBenford's Law, valuation smoothing, window dressing, price divergence numbers that look fabricated or smoothed rather than market-marked
    Portfoliophantom assets, concentration, reconciliation, cost basis assets that don't exist in registries, or portfolios that don't add up
    Structurecircular flow, layered funds, shell networks, cross-fund issuer, peer comparison patterns matched against the documented Banco Master/REAG scheme

    What's actually been measured

    A synthetic-data eval harness (evals/) injects labeled fraud into 4 of 40 funds per signal and checks recall and false-positive rate against the other 36 clean funds. Recall is 100% on every signal tested; false-positive rate on the clean synthetic funds ranges 0–10%. That is real evidence the core logic works — but it is a synthetic universe, not real CVM data, where legitimate funds have structural quirks (feeder/master fund families, illiquid credit, small AUM) a synthetic fixture doesn't reproduce.

    A known false-positive source, and the fix

    An early full-manager run flagged 90 of 94 funds (96%) at a major, reputable administrator — almost all on concentration_violations, because a feeder fund (FIC) legitimately holding ~100% of its portfolio in its single master fund's cotas was scored against the same 20–25% single-issuer limit that applies to a direct-portfolio fund. That is standard, CVM-permitted architecture, not a diversification failure.

    The concentration detector now recognizes a top holding that is itself another fund's CNPJ and excludes it from the regulatory-limit, HHI and top-5 checks — the same treatment phantom_assets_by_fund already gives ordinary fund-of-fund holdings. A fund concentrated in something that is not a fund cota is still flagged normally.

    Reading a flag

    Investigate means strong signals (HIGH/CRITICAL) in at least two independent evidence families. Review means one strong family, or several weaker ones. Neither means fraud — every detector here produces a lead, not proof, and needs corroboration this toolkit cannot see: subscription ledgers, bank transfers, counterparty documentation.
